mbm-2976.clue: The last square gets all the pockets.
mbm-2976.quote: I saved little cloth scraps in the pockets of a work apron. When I finally made the quilt there was nothing left for the final square. I cut out the apron pocket and gave the whole pile a home.

mbm-2977.clue: Our dice travel by cable car.
mbm-2977.quote: I stretched a thread between two chair backs and hung a paper cup from it. Our board-game dice ride across to the next player. We play fewer turns per hour and get much better service.

mbm-2978.clue: I always check under the chairs after the end credits.
mbm-2978.quote: Our anime club paid for its first projector by holding a swap night. We traded cartoons, biscuits and a desk lamp missing its shade. Under the last chair I found a tiny folded paper projector with a coin tucked inside. That one went in our display case.

mbm-2979.clue: I save a little chalk for the walk home.
mbm-2979.quote: At the wall I work on one move until I can close my eyes and feel it. Outside I draw the shape of the holds in chalk on my flat doorstep. I can think through the route while I look for my keys.

mbm-2980.clue: The boundary is a belt with a lucky buckle.
mbm-2980.quote: We forgot the rope for our beach volleyball court once and used everyone's belts. Mine marked the corner. Ever since, when a serve just catches the line, my team thanks the buckle.

mbm-2981.clue: I learned to juggle to a clock with no hands.
mbm-2981.quote: My uncle's old kitchen clock still ticked after its hands fell off. I timed my throws to its patient little beat. We can tell how long I've practiced by the pile of bruised apples.

mbm-2982.clue: I keep the slowest picture of my fastest run.
mbm-2982.quote: My nephew borrowed the camera to photograph me on water skis. He turned it straight toward the wake instead. When we got the film back, one little duck had sailed into the last frame, riding the smallest wave I made. I keep that one on my desk.

mbm-2983.clue: My last set is for the empty bar.
mbm-2983.quote: I finish lifting by practicing one smooth motion with the plates set on the floor. The bar looks light but I pay more attention to it than anything else. That's the part I draw in my training diary.

mbm-2984.clue: I can pick our sandals out by ear.
mbm-2984.quote: After a long soak my friend and I shuffled toward the veranda in the inn's wooden sandals. One of mine clicked twice for every step. The innkeeper tucked a folded slip under the loose strap. I asked to keep the slip; it's the quietest souvenir I own.

mbm-2985.clue: My first encore was one word long.
mbm-2985.quote: At rehearsal we couldn't remember the last verse, so I held one word while the drummer passed a pencil round. Everyone wrote a line on the set list. That much-folded sheet is our favorite song.

mbm-2986.clue: I let my little sister design the shield.
mbm-2986.quote: My little sister drew a spiral staircase on the shield of my homemade card champion. My friends asked where it led. She climbed onto a chair and pointed to the next expansion, which apparently lives on top of the fridge.

mbm-2987.clue: My quilt opens like a family album.
mbm-2987.quote: I sewed three cloth flaps over little embroidered scenes: our porch, a fishing pier and a kitchen chair. My grandfather lifts the chair flap first. That's where I hid the little orange cat we both remember.
